description:
Surfaced while building String.Chars for fz-5xp.15. PRE-EXISTING and general --
it is not specific to the new protocol.

    Enum.count(:not_enumerable)     # Enumerable has no impl for Atom
    Enum.count({1, 2})              # nor for Tuple
    to_string(%{a: 1})              # StringChars has no impl for Map

All three:

    thread 'main' panicked at src/compiler2/jobs/artifact.rs:142:6:
    product materialization should have complete call edges after waits

An internal assertion, with no span, no code, and no mention of the protocol or
the receiver.

WHY THIS BLOCKS fz-5xp.15. That ticket's main design point is that Elixir gives
`String.Chars` NO `@fallback_to_any` on purpose: interpolating a map or a tuple
RAISES rather than printing something structural, and the ticket says "in fz it
becomes panic". A panic is a defined outcome a program can be written against.
An ICE is not: the compiler falls over before the program exists. So the safety
property fz-5xp.15 exists to preserve cannot currently be expressed.

Elixir, for comparison:

    ** (Protocol.UndefinedError) protocol String.Chars not implemented for
       %{a: 1} of type Map

WHAT THE ANSWER PROBABLY IS. The receiver's type is known at the call: the
`artifact.rs:142` assertion fires because dispatch found no impl and left the
call edge incomplete, which every later stage assumes cannot happen. Where the
receiver type is ground, "no impl for this protocol and this type" is decidable
at compile time and deserves a real diagnostic with the callsite's span, naming
the protocol and the type -- better than Elixir, which can only raise at
runtime. Where the receiver is a union that MIGHT have an impl, the arm with no
impl has to become a runtime panic.

DONE = the three calls above each produce a diagnostic (ground receiver) or a
runtime panic (union receiver) naming the protocol and the receiver type, on all
three doors, with a fixture. The `artifact.rs:142` assertion should then be
unreachable for this reason.
title: [BUG] A protocol call with no matching impl is a compiler ICE, not a diagnostic
